title: Genome-Wide CRISPR Screen Identifies GJB2 and BET1L as Barriers to Editing Efficiency
detail: A six-year project led by Professor Krishanu Saha at the University of Wisconsin–Madison screened more than 19,000 human genes to find cellular factors that impede nonviral CRISPR genome editing, published in Nature Communications. The team narrowed 19,144 candidate genes to 26 whose disruption improved editing efficiency, then validated two — GJB2 and BET1L — whose knockout boosted base-editor efficiency more than sixfold in human model cell systems. In patient-derived retinal cells carrying mutations for Leber congenital amaurosis, inhibiting the two genes more than tripled gene-editing efficiency, suggesting transient co-suppression of these genes as a strategy to improve delivery and efficacy of future CRISPR gene therapies.

title: Caribou Biosciences Reports Q2 2026: Vispa-Cel 82% ORR in Lymphoma, CB-011 92% ORR in Myeloma
detail: Caribou Biosciences' Q2 2026 business update reported updated ANTLER trial data for vispacabtagene regedleucel (vispa-cel), a CRISPR-edited allogeneic CD19 CAR-T therapy for second-line large B-cell lymphoma: an 82% overall response rate, 67% complete response rate, and 17.1-month median progression-free survival among 27 optimized-regimen patients treated with a single 80-million-cell dose. In the CaMMouflage trial, CB-011 (allogeneic BCMA-targeted CAR-T for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma) achieved a 92% overall response rate, 83% rate of ≥CR, and 91% MRD-negativity among 12 BCMA-naive patients at the 450-million-cell dose, with initial dose-expansion data expected in H2 2026. The company reported a $24.3 million GAAP net loss for the quarter and $113.8 million in cash, funding operations into the end of 2027.
